newsitem.title: NORWAY: ALPINE SKIING-STROBL WINS, ALPHAND DENIED SECOND TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-STROBL WINS, ALPHAND DENIED SECOND TITLE.

text.p: Austrian Josef Strobl collected his first World Cup super-G victory on Sunday while Luc Alphand was denied his second title of the day by one-hundredth of a second.

Frenchman Alphand, who began the day by clinching his third consecutive World Cup downhill crown, missed out on a double success when he finished in a tie for fourth with Austria's Herrmann Maier in the super-G.
After a steady downpour had twice delayed the start, the skies suddenly cleared, allowing officials to proceed with the second race of the day.
Ignoring the soggy conditions Strobl, sloshed his way down the slushy 2,418-metre Olympiabakken course in a time of one minute 24.95 seconds to claim his third career win.
Austria's Andreas Schifferer was second in 1:25.63 while Norway's Lasse Kjus, who hours earlier had won the downhill, returned to the podium taking third in 1:25.87.
Maier and Alphand were deadlocked in fourth with 1:26.02. The Frenchman will now have to wait to the World Cup finals in Vail in two weeks to see if he can add the super-G title to his collection.
